name: manual_848da335af02
claim: Representation-boundary correction to lesson_f6cbb9825f37: JSON serialization itself CAN preserve a trailing LF inside a string value -- it is not a lossy boundary. The actual lossy boundary in the recorded incident was the shell/CLI layer: `printf '%s\n'` appended the local LF and Bash command substitution in the CLI/readback path stripped it. Exact-byte hashing remains correct for Git blobs, tracked files, and binary transport, and remains wrong for mutable external text fields (GitHub PR/issue bodies) -- but the misidentified root cause is the shell/command-substitution boundary, not JSON serialization. Prefer content-hash or canonicalized-comparison for external text fields; do not attribute loss to JSON.
